# ForgeOS v0.4 Production Federation Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build a production-oriented ForgeOS federation layer that safely resolves 1,024 typed capabilities to first-party skills, third-party Agent Skills, authoritative knowledge, and MCP servers.

**Architecture:** Preserve the v0.3 Trust Kernel. Add a metadata-first federation control plane with immutable source coordinates, trust receipts, semantic deduplication, provider resolution, and fail-closed promotion. Keep network and storage behind dependency-injected interfaces so all trust logic is deterministic and testable offline.

**Tech Stack:** Node.js 20+ ESM, built-in Web Crypto and Fetch, JSON Schema draft 2020-12, MCP/A2A interfaces already present, SQL reference migrations, Node test runner.

## Global Constraints

- No third-party skill or MCP server is executable during discovery or import.
- No remote provider becomes active without pinned provenance, policy pass, evaluation receipt, and administrator approval.
- Keep all existing v0.3 public lifecycle behavior and tests.
- Use canonical JSON and SHA-256 for immutable identities.
- Do not copy external proprietary documentation into the repository; store references and licensing metadata.
- Treat popularity as discovery metadata, never as a trust decision.
- Generate no claim that 1,024 capabilities equal 1,024 locally authored expert prompts.
- Every new public tool must have strict input/output schemas and a full MCP lifecycle test.
